en: concerning the conduct of the four social classes (*cāturvarṇya-ācāra*): in the Kali age, the *Smṛti* of Parāśara is prescribed.
Those who are deprived of the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice and excluded from hospitality—
all of them go to hell and enter the womb of a crow.
Even if he is a sinner, an outcaste, a slayer of Brahmins, or a murderer of his father— if such a person arrives during the Vaiśvadeva rite, he is a guest who leads one to heaven.
He who eats with his head wrapped, he who eats facing south,
or he who places his hand upon his left foot— verily, the Rākṣasas consume that food.
The section on expiation consists of the purification of substances and the two types of fire-rites.
by that blood and that impurity, all of them have been satiated.

(He shakes off [his sins]; having bathed, the twice-born man purifies himself: "The sacred fords beginning with Prabhāsa, as well as the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā. (Parāśara 12.20ab). (This line is not in the BI edition).
"In the right ear of a Brahmin they exist," so Manu has declared.
(Not in BI ed. The Maruts, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas are indeed the deities. (māruto) He shall thus purify himself both in this world and in the next. (BI: he shall burn [his sins])
No sūtra on *vyavahāra* (found only in the *Parāśaramādhava*)...
